hotspots.tagline: Free adaptive skating on DCR ice, two inclusive waterfront playgrounds, and some of the country's best children's hospitals a short ride away.
highlights: Boston Children's Hospital, Franciscan Children's (pediatric rehab in Brighton) and Shriners Children's Boston are all in the city
Spaulding Adaptive Sports Centers runs the Sledgehogs youth sled hockey team, and the state's DCR Universal Access Program offers free adaptive ice skating with sleds and skate walkers in East Boston
Martin's Park in the Seaport and the fully ADA-accessible Gronk Playground on the Esplanade were built for kids of all abilities
Free equipment help: Easterseals Massachusetts' Assistive Technology Regional Center lends devices for up to 30 days, and REquipment gives away refurbished wheelchairs and other gear
pediatric_hospitals: Franciscan Children's (Brighton; pediatric rehabilitation, a Boston Children's affiliate)
inclusive_playgrounds: Martin's Park at Children's Wharf Park in the Seaport (sloped paths reach the top of the play areas)
Gronk Playground on the Charles River Esplanade, opened in 2025 as a fully ADA-accessible playground
Ask Boston Parks and Recreation which neighborhood playgrounds near you have rubber surfacing
hotspots.transit_notes: The MBTA says all of its buses and most subway and trolley stations are accessible; call the Elevator/Escalator Hotline (617-222-2828) or check mbta.com accessibility alerts before you head out. The RIDE, the MBTA's door-to-door paratransit, serves 58 greater Boston cities and towns for riders whose disability keeps them from using fixed routes some or all of the time; apply through the MBTA Mobility Center, which also offers free travel training. Brick sidewalks in some historic neighborhoods can be bumpy.
hotspots.waiver_notes: MassHealth covers many children with disabilities; MassHealth CommonHealth is a pathway for children and adults with disabilities who can't get MassHealth Standard, with premiums that depend on income. The Kaileigh Mulligan program lets qualifying children with severe disabilities be cared for at home without counting parental income or assets. Massachusetts Early Intervention serves children birth to three at no out-of-pocket cost, and the Department of Developmental Services (DDS) funds Family Support Centers for eligible families. Ask your hospital social worker which options fit your child.
hotspots.school_notes: Boston Public Schools' specialized services team handles IEPs, Child Find, and transition services. The Boston Special Education Parent Advisory Council (SpEdPAC) holds family meetings and trainings, and the Federation for Children with Special Needs, Massachusetts' Parent Training and Information Center, offers free help understanding IEPs and special education rights.

insider_tips.tip: The four accessible parking spaces on the Esplanade are at the Blossom Street entrance, between Teddy Ebersol's Red Sox Fields and the Alfond Spray Deck, close to the Gronk Playground.
Kids who use their own wheelchair get into the New England Aquarium free, and visitors with visual impairments do too.
At the Museum of Science, personal care assistants get in free, and the museum lends pediatric wheelchairs at no charge.
Want to try a communication device or adapted toy before you buy? Borrow it free for up to 30 days from the Easterseals Assistive Technology Regional Center on South Street in Boston.

watch_outs: Snow and ice can block curb cuts in winter
Brick sidewalks in historic neighborhoods are bumpy
Station elevators sometimes go out of service, so check before you travel

hotspots.tagline: Lake loops for rolling, a children's museum where every exhibit welcomes wheelchairs, and youth wheelchair basketball with national titles.
highlights: Gillette Children's in St. Paul is a specialty children's hospital with a Cerebral Palsy Institute; Children's Minnesota and M Health Fairview Masonic Children's Hospital are in Minneapolis
Courage Kenny Adaptive Sports & Recreation in Golden Valley runs youth wheelchair basketball teams, power soccer, and more, with a cost share/scholarship option
PACER Center in Bloomington is Minnesota's federally designated Parent Training and Information Center and runs a free-for-Minnesotans assistive technology lending library
Metro Transit light rail boards step-free, and Metro Mobility provides ADA paratransit across the metro
pediatric_hospitals: Children's Minnesota (Minneapolis and St. Paul hospitals)
M Health Fairview University of Minnesota Masonic Children's Hospital (Minneapolis)
inclusive_playgrounds: Wabun Universal Access Play Area at Minnehaha Regional Park (Minneapolis' first universally accessible play area)
P.K.'s Place next to Allianz Field in St. Paul's Midway, with ramps up to the central play structure
Madison's Place in Woodbury, a fully inclusive playground at the Bielenberg Sports Center
Rosland Park in Edina, whose main structure is accessible all the way to the top
hotspots.transit_notes: Metro Transit light rail offers step-free boarding and priority seating, and buses lower a ramp (wait 7 to 10 feet back from the curb so it can deploy). Metro Mobility is the Metropolitan Council's ADA paratransit service: apply with a two-part form that includes professional verification, and expect an eligibility decision within about 21 days.
hotspots.waiver_notes: Minnesota's Medical Assistance under the TEFRA option lets children under 19 with a certified disability qualify based on the child's own income, and Minnesota stopped charging parental fees for TEFRA and home and community-based services on July 1, 2023. Eligibility for the disability waivers (including CAC, CADI, DD, and BI) is decided through a MnCHOICES assessment with your county, and Community First Services and Supports (CFSS) is replacing PCA and the Consumer Support Grant. The Family Support Grant can help eligible families who aren't on a waiver or PCA with costs such as respite. In Hennepin County, ask the county's disability services Front Door line where to start.
hotspots.school_notes: Help Me Grow is Minnesota's free referral door for children birth to 5; local school districts run Infant and Toddler Intervention and Preschool Special Education. Minneapolis Public Schools' Special Education Department handles evaluations and IEPs and has a Special Education Advisory Council (SEAC) for families. PACER Center is the free Parent Training and Information Center and helps families get ready for IEP meetings.

insider_tips.tip: Lake Harriet's paved walking path is about 2.75 miles around, with a separate bike path, so little wheels and big wheels each get their own lane.
At Minnesota Children's Museum, ask the box office for noise-reducing headphones, visual timers, or universal cuffs; personal care attendants get in free with the person they assist.
Request Minneapolis Parks inclusion support at least two weeks before a program starts.
Three Rivers Park District keeps child-size all-terrain wheelchairs at some nature centers; contact the park early to ask.

watch_outs: Long, cold winters, and some regional park restrooms close for the off-season
Metro Mobility needs an application and eligibility decision before your first ride, so apply early
Family Support Grant funding is limited and there may be a waiting list

hotspots.tagline: Free adaptive bikes by the lake, youth wheelchair basketball with chairs provided, and a top children's hospital in town.
highlights: Seattle Children's Hospital has a Rehabilitation Medicine program, a Tone Management Program for spasticity and dystonia, and inpatient rehabilitation for patients up to age 21
Outdoors for All lends adaptive bikes free of charge for on-site rides at its Magnuson Park Adaptive Cycling Center during the warm-weather season
Seattle Adaptive Sports runs youth wheelchair basketball (they provide the chairs), a youth sled hockey team, and power soccer
Seattle Parks and Recreation's Specialized Programs offer day camps for ages 4-21, youth weekend trips, and teen and young adult afterschool programs
inclusive_playgrounds: Seattle Children's PlayGarden at Colman Playground in South Seattle: a free, fenced, fully accessible park with turf surfacing and low, wide play structures
Inspiration Playground at Bellevue Downtown Park, a universally accessible playground built by the City of Bellevue with the Bellevue Rotary Club
hotspots.transit_notes: Every King County Metro bus has a wheelchair lift or ramp, and Sound Transit's Link light rail offers level boarding, with elevators at stations above or below street level. King County Metro's Access Transportation is the ADA paratransit service for riders ages 6 and up whose disability keeps them from using buses and light rail on their own; qualifying with one Puget Sound agency lets you ride with the others in the regional agreement. Seattle is hilly, so plan routes around the steepest streets.
hotspots.waiver_notes: Washington Apple Health for Kids gives children under 19 medical, dental, vision, and mental health coverage (free or low-cost depending on household income, with no deductibles or co-pays). The DSHS Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA, briefly called DDCS in 2025) offers services for eligible children and youth ages 0-21 and Home and Community Based waivers such as Basic Plus. For babies and toddlers, Washington's Early Support for Infants and Toddlers (ESIT) program at DCYF serves children from birth to age 3. Unpaid family caregivers can also apply for a Lifespan Respite Washington voucher.
hotspots.school_notes: Seattle Public Schools' Special Education department builds each student's IEP with the family and has a district ombudsperson for concerns not settled at school. PAVE is Washington's Parent Training and Information Center and gives free help preparing for IEP and 504 meetings, and the parent-led Seattle Special Education PTSA publishes a guide to special education in ten languages.

insider_tips.tip: Green Lake's 2.8-mile paved inner loop has an outside lane just for wheels, and motorized wheelchairs are the only motorized devices allowed on the path.
Seattle Adaptive Sports invites families to a training session to try a sport; kids don't need to use a wheelchair every day to play wheelchair basketball, and the team provides the chairs.
At Pacific Science Center, a guest's aide gets complimentary admission, and free wheelchairs and sensory kits are available at the Main Entry.
Seattle Parks' Specialized Programs say they accept DDA (DDCS) respite funds for camp where applicable, so ask your case manager before you register.

watch_outs: Many outdoor programs (adaptive cycling, spray features, summer camps) are seasonal, so register early
DDA eligibility and enrollment can take time, so start early
